title: Retention simulator + Deletion Saga Orchestrator for analytics pipelines
creator: Morgan Rivera
description:
Background: As the Console's telemetry and usage analytics grow, we need a demonstrable, auditable deletion flow that accounts for data stored across multiple backends (event store, aggregated OLAP, long-term cold storage) while minimizing disruption to downstream dashboards and internally-run ML features. Current one-off deletion scripts are hard to reason about, risk missing derived aggregates, and don't provide good preflight validation for legal/DSR requests.

Goal: Build two complementary pieces: (1) a retention simulator that models retention windows, cascade deletes, and query fallout so product and legal can preview impact of a proposed deletion policy; (2) a Deletion Saga Orchestrator that executes multi-step deletions across systems with idempotency, audit trails, retry/backoff semantics, and an attestable proof-of-deletion artifact.

Success criteria / acceptance criteria:
- Retention simulator can run a policy preview against a one-week sample window and produce: expected row counts removed per system, downstream metric deltas for top 10 dashboards, and a risk score for missing joins.
- Orchestrator implements a durable saga pattern with per-step compensation actions, maintains an immutable audit-log entry for each request, and exposes a signed deletion attestation (hash + timestamp + components affected).
- End-to-end test that triggers a synthetic DSR and verifies artifacts in audit log, tombstone markers, and removal from the UI-facing aggregates within SLO (24h for full pipeline backfills).
- Metrics and alerts for stuck sagas, per-tenant deletion rate, and estimated backlog.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Strong vs eventual enforcement: we chose eventual consistency for aggregated tables to avoid hammering OLAP during mass deletions; the simulator reports expected time-to-completion and transient metric anomalies so PMs/legal can weigh tolerances.
- Idempotency: use a global deletion request id (UUID v4) persisted in the orchestrator DB and echoed to each downstream adapter to deduplicate retries.
- Compensation vs hard rollback: for some sinks (S3 cold archives, audit exports) a true rollback is impossible; instead we emit a compensation event that marks derived datasets as stale and triggers rebuilds.
- Privacy surface: mapping from user_id -> ephemeral pseudomap stored in ephemeral-keystore with TTL; the orchestrator only sends ephemeral tokens to downstream systems when needed. The simulator can optionally run in 'privacy-strict' mode where pseudomaps are not used, showing worst-case impact.

Components to implement:
1) retention-simulator service (Go): sample ingestion, policy DSL eval, quick Monte Carlo to surface risks, HTTP UI endpoint returning JSON report + CSV artifacts.
2) saga-orchestrator service (Python): durable state machine, per-adapter connectors (Clickhouse, Redshift, S3, BigQuery, Console events API), audit-log writer, signed attestation generator (using KMS).
3) Connectors/adapters: thin idempotent wrappers each with test harness.
4) E2E test harness: infra job that provisions sample data and asserts deletion end-state.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1 (Feb 17-23): proto retention simulator that runs locally on sample data; define policy DSL and report schema.
- Week 2: basic orchestrator skeleton with persistent requests table, basic Clickhouse adapter, and audit-log writer.
- Week 3: connectors for S3 + OLAP, attestation signing, CI for idempotency tests.
- Week 4: run e2e tests, add monitoring, and prepare runbook + playbook.

Rollout & compliance considerations:
- Default: simulator opt-in for PM/legal. Orchestrator accessible via Console for admin users (RBAC gating) and through an internal API for SREs.
- Auditing: every deletion request produces an immutable artifact stored in the compliance bucket; the signed attestation is downloadable as proof for customer DSRs.
- Security review: mandatory before public rollout; KMS integration required for attestation keys.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Retention policy DSL: how expressive do we need (per-customer overrides, dataset-level overrides, event-type conditions)? (PM to decide by 2025-02-20).
- Cold-archive deletion semantics: do we permit delayed physical deletion (e.g., legal hold window) or must attestation always represent logical deletion? Legal to confirm hold behavior.
- SLA for deletion completion for paid tiers (Dedicated customers) vs free-tier: do we prioritize Dedicated in the orchestrator routing?

Related artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://drive.google.com/example-retention-simulator-design
- Console PRD (internal): https://confluence.company/ConsolePrivacy/DeletionSagaPRD
- Prototype simulator repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/retention-simulator/pull/12
- Orchestrator initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/deletion-saga/pull/3

Monitoring and observability:
- New metrics: deletion_requests_total, deletion_request_duration_seconds{status,adapter}, deletion_backlog_per_tenant, deletion_attestations_issued_total.
- Dashboards: console-privacy > Deletion Pipeline (errors, latency, throughput).
- Alerts: alert when any request is > 6h in PENDING state, or when failure rate > 1% for 30m.

Acceptance tests / QA checklist:
- PRs include unit tests for each adapter and integration test for orchestrator state machine.
- Run e2e harness on staging with sampled production-like data (anonymized).
- Legal and Security to run a tabletop exercise verifying attestation artifacts and access controls.

Business impact / rationale:
- Removes manual deletion toil and provides auditable evidence for customer DSRs and regulatory audits.
- Reduces risk of silent leakage where derived analytics were overlooked by ad-hoc scripts.
- Gives PMs/Legal visibility into the expected fallout of policy changes before they go live (reduces rollback incidents).
